record.context_brief: Jensen-type theorem for generalized differential operators
record.original_question:
de Bruijn proved that if a real entire function f has order less than
two and all zeros in the strip S(Δ) = {z ∈ C : |Im
z| ≤ Δ}, then the zeros of cos(λD)f lie in the narrower strip |Im z| ≤
√(Δ^2 - λ^2) when Δ > λ, and are all real when 0
≤ Δ ≤ λ. Determine whether an analogous Jensen-type theorem holds for
φ(λD)f when φ is a more general transcendental
entire function.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let D = d/dx denote ordinary differentiation. For a transcendental entire function φ(z) = Σ a_n z^n and a sufficiently regular entire function f, define the differential operator φ(λD) formally by

  φ(λD)f(x) = Σ_{n≥0} a_n λ^n f^{(n)}(x),

acting on real entire functions f of order less than two for which the series converges to an entire function of x.

A classical theorem of de Bruijn asserts: if f is a real entire function of order less than two whose zeros all lie in the closed strip

  S(Δ) = { z ∈ C : |Im z| ≤ Δ },  Δ ≥ 0,

then, for every λ ≥ 0, the zeros of cos(λD) f(x) = Σ_{n≥0} ((-1)^n λ^{2n}/(2n)!) f^{(2n)}(x) lie in the strip |Im z| ≤ √(Δ² − λ²) when Δ > λ, and are all real when 0 ≤ Δ ≤ λ.

Problem. Determine, for which transcendental entire functions φ, an analogous Jensen-type theorem holds for the operator φ(λD). More precisely, characterize the entire functions φ such that there exists a function Δ ↦ Δ'(Δ, λ) ≥ 0 (with Δ'(Δ, λ) ≤ Δ, and equal to 0 for λ sufficiently large relative to Δ) with the property that whenever f is a real entire function of order less than two with all zeros in S(Δ), the zeros of φ(λD)f all lie in S(Δ'(Δ, λ)).
artifact.category_tag: Zeros of entire functions and differential operators
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is listed as an open problem in the AIM workshop list on Pólya–Schur–Lax problems (Problem 32, citing an earlier open-problem collection). Web searches do not reveal a published resolution of the general φ(λD) analogue of de Bruijn's theorem; results in the literature concentrate on specific multipliers (cosine, Gaussian heat-kernel as in the de Bruijn–Newman constant work) rather than a general characterization.
